examples.en: I subscribe to a newspaper every morning.
I subscribed to my favorite channel.
Many people subscribe to this magazine.

examples.ko: 구독하면 새 영상이 올라올 때 알림이 와요.
examples.en: If you subscribe, you get a notification when a new video is posted.
I will subscribe for just one month.
If you do not use a service you subscribed to, cancel it.

explain: 구독하다는 신문·잡지처럼 정기적으로 받아 보려고 신청할 때 쓰고, 요즘은 유튜브 채널이나 음악·영상 서비스에도 써요. '구독하다'의 목적어는 '채널을', '신문을'처럼 '을/를'이에요. 그만둘 때는 '구독을 취소하다', '구독을 해지하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I signed up to subscribe to the channel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구독을 시작하려고 신청하는 단계를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the step of signing up to start a subscription.
phrases.en_equiv: to sign up for a subscription

phrases.en: I stopped watching it, so I cancelled my subscription.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구독을 그만둘 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The standard phrase for ending a subscription.

phrases.en: I have been subscribed to that magazine for three years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속 받아 보고 있다는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the ongoing state of currently subscribing.

explain_en: Regularly receive a publication or channel (잡지를 구독하다) 구독하다 means signing up to receive something regularly, like a newspaper or magazine, and today also YouTube channels and music or video services. The object takes 을/를, as in '채널을 구독하다'. To stop, say '구독을 취소하다' or '구독을 해지하다'.

en: to raise; to make something go up

examples.en: The government decided to raise interest rates.

examples.ko: 이 약은 체온을 상승시킬 수 있어요.
examples.en: This medicine can raise body temperature.
A good ad pushed sales up.
Exercise lifts your mood.
If you raise the price, customers decrease.

examples.ko: 회사의 가치를 상승시킨 사람은 새 대표예요.
examples.en: The person who raised the company's value is the new CEO.

explain: '올리다'와 가깝지만 더 딱딱해서 뉴스, 경제, 보고서에 어울려요. 저절로 오르는 것은 '상승하다', 올리는 사람이 있으면 '상승시키다'예요. 반대말은 '하락시키다'예요.

phrases.en: The store raised its prices.
phrases.nuance_ko: '상승시키다'보다 쉽고 일상적이에요. 말할 때는 보통 '올리다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is simpler and more everyday than '상승시키다'. In speech people usually say '올리다'.

phrases.en: A heater raises the room temperature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 온도, 가격, 수치처럼 올라가는 것을 받아서 써요. 설명하는 글에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: It takes things that go up, like temperature, prices, or numbers. It fits explanatory writing.

phrases.en: Prices keep rising.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저절로 오를 때 써요. 올리는 사람이 있으면 '상승시키다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when something rises on its own. If someone raises it, use '상승시키다'.

explain_en: Formal causative; things like temperature or levels, written style. It is close to '올리다' but stiffer, so it suits news, economics, and reports. Something that rises by itself is '상승하다'; when someone causes the rise, use '상승시키다'. The opposite is '하락시키다'.

examples.en: The company became a sponsor of the competition.
We could not find a sponsor, so the event was scaled down.

examples.ko: 스폰서 덕분에 무료로 열 수 있었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the sponsor, we could hold it for free.

examples.ko: 이 팀의 스폰서는 유명한 음료 회사예요.
examples.en: This team's sponsor is a famous beverage company.
We passed on our thanks to the sponsor.
We signed a contract with a new sponsor.

explain: '후원자', '후원하다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요. 방송이나 행사에서는 '협찬'이라는 말도 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: This event has many sponsors.
phrases.nuance_ko: '스폰서'와 같은 뜻의 한자어로, 일상에서 두루 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A Sino-Korean word with the same meaning as 'sponsor', used widely in everyday speech.

phrases.en: The team is looking for a new sponsor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 도와줄 곳이 필요할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when someone needs a party to fund them.

phrases.en: The company sponsors our team.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스폰서가 하는 일을 동사로 말한 거예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb for what a sponsor does.

explain_en: 'Huwonja' and 'huwonhada' are used too. In broadcasts and events you also see the word 'hyeopchan'.

en: to be provided; to be offered; to receive

examples.ko: 공사 현장 일꾼은 숙식을 제공받아서 월급을 거의 모았다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the construction workers got room and board, so they saved almost all their pay.
I get lunch provided by my company.
I was provided with a laptop by my school.

examples.ko: 이 앱으로 실시간 교통 정보를 제공받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: With this app you can receive real-time traffic information.

examples.ko: 무료로 제공받은 쿠폰은 이번 달까지 써야 해요.
examples.en: The coupon I got for free has to be used by the end of this month.

examples.ko: 서비스를 제공받으려면 먼저 회원 가입을 하세요.
examples.en: To receive the service, please sign up as a member first.

explain: 주는 쪽은 '제공하다', 받는 쪽은 '제공받다'예요. '회사에서 숙소를 제공받다'처럼 '-에서/-에게 ~을 제공받다'로 써요. 말할 때는 '(무료로) 받다'로 바꿔도 되지만 '제공받다'가 공식적인 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I was provided with a school uniform by the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형이에요. 이미 받은 일을 공식적인 느낌으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the past tense, saying what you already received in a formal tone.

phrases.example: 신청하면 책을 무료로 제공받을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you apply, you can receive a book for free.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 내지 않고 받을 때 '무료로'와 자주 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is often used with 무료로 when you get something without paying.

phrases.example: 회원은 교육 자료를 제공받을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Members can be provided with training materials.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받을 수 있는 혜택이나 조건을 안내할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to explain a benefit or condition someone can receive.

explain_en: Receiver's viewpoint: getting something supplied or offered to you. '제공하다' is for the giver and '제공받다' is for the receiver. Use it like '회사에서 숙소를 제공받다', with -에서/-에게 marking the source. In casual speech you can say '(무료로) 받다' instead, but '제공받다' sounds more formal.

t90.ax: I get lunch provided by my company.

en: to increase; to enhance; to raise

examples.en: Exercise increases strength.
The company increased production this year.

examples.ko: 홍보를 늘리면 손님을 증가시킬 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you do more promotion, you can bring in more customers.
They say vitamins boost immunity.
I oppose policies that raise taxes.
I increased practice time, and my skills improved.

explain: 사람이나 원인이 직접 양을 늘리는 쪽이에요. 스스로 늘어난 것은 '증가하다', 누가 늘린 것은 '증가시키다'라고 해서 짝이 돼요. 일상에서는 '늘리다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The company lengthened working hours.
phrases.nuance_ko: '증가시키다'보다 일상에서 자연스러운 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more natural, easy word than '증가시키다' in daily life.

phrases.example: 이 방법은 수입을 증가시킬 수 있어요.
phrases.en: This method can increase income.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 방법이나 원인이 늘리는 힘이 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a method or cause is able to increase something.

phrases.en: Your strength increases when you exercise.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 늘린 것이 아니라 스스로 늘어난 것을 말할 때 써서 짝이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with this word for something that increases by itself, not by someone's action.

explain_en: Formal; cause a number or level to rise (체력을 증가시키다) Here a person or cause directly makes an amount grow. It pairs with '증가하다' for things that grow on their own. In everyday speech, '늘리다' sounds more natural.

dis.h: formal: cause a number to rise

p.n: Same meaning; the native verb sounds more casual.

en: to be improved; to be reformed

examples.en: My health improved after I took the medicine.
The service is getting better little by little.
If the environment improves, more people gather.
I can see the parts that are improving.
This problem needs to be improved quickly.
I hope the mood in the room gets much better.

explain: 나쁜 부분이 좋아질 때 써요. 상태, 제도, 서비스처럼 고칠 수 있는 것에 어울려요. 날씨나 기분이 좋아질 때는 '좋아지다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 우리 동네 버스 서비스가 점점 개선되고 있어요.
phrases.en: The bus service in our town is improving little by little.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋아지는 일이 지금 이어지고 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when the improvement is still going on.

phrases.example: 새 규칙 덕분에 환경이 크게 개선됐어요.
phrases.en: Thanks to the new rule, the environment improved a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '크게'를 붙이면 많이 좋아졌다는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '크게' means it got much better.

phrases.en: I feel a little better than yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '개선되다'보다 쉽고 일상에서 써요. 몸이나 기분에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more everyday than '개선되다'. It also works for health or mood.

explain_en: Passive — conditions or systems get better (도로가 개선되다) Use it when a weak part gets better. It fits things you can fix, such as conditions, systems, or services. For weather or mood, say '좋아지다'.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 최근 몇 년 사이 급성장했어요.
examples.en: This city has grown rapidly in the past few years.
The delivery market is growing rapidly.
A rapidly growing company hires many employees.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 입소문 덕분에 급성장할 거예요.
examples.en: Thanks to word of mouth, this shop will grow fast.

examples.ko: 관광객이 늘면서 이 지역이 급성장해서 집값이 올랐어요.
examples.en: As tourists increased, this area grew rapidly and housing prices rose.

examples.ko: 급성장한 만큼 해결할 문제도 많이 생겼어요.
examples.en: Because it grew so fast, many problems to solve have come up.

explain: '급성장하다'는 '빠르게 성장하다'를 한 단어로 줄인 느낌이고, 시장, 기업, 지역처럼 사람이 아닌 대상에 많이 써요. 사람이 빨리 자랄 때는 '쑥쑥 자라다' 같은 쉬운 표현이 어울려요. 명사 '급성장'에 '하다'가 붙은 말이라 '급성장을 하다'로도 써요.

phrases.en: I want to work at a rapidly growing company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때는 '급성장하는'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '급성장하는' to describe the noun that follows.

phrases.en: The shop grew rapidly, so they are hiring more staff.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠르게 커진 일이 이유가 되어 다음 일이 생길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when fast growth is the reason for what comes next.

phrases.en: This city is growing quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '급성장하다'를 풀어서 쓴 말로 조금 더 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: This spells out '급성장하다' and is a little easier to say.

explain_en: 급성장하다 is like a one-word shortening of 빠르게 성장하다, and it is mostly used for non-person subjects such as markets, companies and regions. When a person grows quickly, an easier expression like 쑥쑥 자라다 fits better. It is the noun 급성장 plus 하다, so 급성장을 하다 is also possible.

en: to nurture; to bring up; to take care of

examples.ko: 이 어린이집은 아이를 하루 종일 보육해요.
examples.en: This daycare cares for children all day.

examples.ko: 맞벌이 부부를 위해 회사가 직원 자녀를 보육해 줘요.
examples.en: The company looks after employees' children for dual-income couples.
The government helps with the cost of caring for children.

examples.ko: 저는 아기를 보육하는 선생님이 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to become a teacher who takes care of babies.

examples.ko: 새 센터에서 아기를 보육할 선생님을 구하고 있어요.
examples.en: The new center is looking for teachers to care for babies.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 아이를 잘 보육하면 건강하게 자라요.
examples.en: If you care for a child well when young, they grow up healthy.

explain: 어린아이를 돌보고 키울 때 쓰는 공식적인 말이에요. 집에서 부모가 아기를 키울 때는 '키우다', '돌보다'를 더 많이 말해요. '보육'은 어린이집과 나라 정책 이야기에서 주로 나와요.

phrases.example: 이 센터는 아기 열 명을 보육하고 있어요.
phrases.en: This center is taking care of ten babies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기관이 계속해서 아이를 돌보고 있다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means an institution is continuously caring for children.

phrases.en: There is a childcare facility near my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어린이집처럼 아이를 돌보는 곳을 말하는 공식적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal term for places that care for children, like daycare.

phrases.en: Grandmother looks after her grandchild during the day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 아이를 볼 때는 '보육하다'보다 '돌보다'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: At home, 돌보다 sounds more natural than 보육하다.

explain_en: A formal word for looking after and raising small children. At home, parents say '키우다' or '돌보다'. '보육' mainly appears with daycares and government policy.

examples.en: I will establish a company next year.

examples.ko: 이 학교는 백 년 전에 한 선교사가 설립했어요.
examples.en: A missionary founded this school a hundred years ago.

examples.ko: 친구와 같이 작은 출판사를 설립하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to found a small publishing company with a friend.
The person who set up the foundation was a teacher.
There is a plan to establish a new library.
You need documents to establish an organization.

explain: 회사, 학교, 단체처럼 공식적인 조직을 새로 세울 때 써요. 집이나 건물은 '짓다'를 쓰고, 가게를 여는 것은 '차리다'나 '열다'를 더 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: I started a company with my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '설립하다'와 뜻이 같지만 말할 때 더 쉽고 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning but easier and more natural in speech.

phrases.en: The person who founded this group is a doctor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '설립한'은 만든 사람이나 때를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe who or when something was founded.

phrases.en: I plan to found a small school next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 할 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about future plans.

explain_en: Found a school, company or institution; formal. It is used when you newly set up an official organization such as a company, school or group. For houses and buildings use '짓다', and for opening a shop '차리다' or '열다' is more common.

t90.ax: I will establish a company next year.

examples.en: The village patrol goes around the alleys every night.
Crime has dropped thanks to the patrol team.
A parent patrol watches over the route to school.

examples.ko: 순찰대는 이상한 사람을 보면 바로 신고해요.
examples.en: The patrol reports right away if they see a suspicious person.
The beach patrol keeps an eye on the swimmers.
A volunteer patrol was formed in our neighborhood too.

explain: '순찰대'는 경찰이 아니어도 동네 사람들이 자원해서 만들 수 있어요. 경찰이 타고 다니는 차는 '순찰차', 돌아다니며 살피는 일은 '순찰하다'라고 해요. 이 세 단어를 같이 기억해 두면 편해요.

phrases.en: The police patrol the neighborhood every night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순찰대가 하는 일을 말하는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb for what a patrol team does.

phrases.en: A patrol car is parked at the entrance of the alley.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경찰이 타고 다니는 차를 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for the car police drive around in.

phrases.example: 저도 이번 달부터 마을 순찰대에 참여해요.
phrases.en: I'm joining the neighborhood patrol team this month too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자원해서 동네 순찰대에 들어가는 상황에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits the situation of volunteering to join a local patrol team.

explain_en: A patrol group of people, not a vehicle (순찰대를 꾸리다) A 순찰대 does not have to be police; neighbors can form one as volunteers. The car police patrol in is a 순찰차, and the act of going around and watching is 순찰하다. It helps to remember these three words together.

examples.en: The two companies made the film as a joint venture.
It is a joint Korea-Japan drama.
This album is a collaboration between two singers.
They decided to set up a joint company.
This painting is a work the brothers made together.
We are looking into a joint investment.

explain: 나라나 회사가 함께 만들 때 '합작 영화', '합작 회사'처럼 앞에 붙여요. '협력'은 서로 돕는 것 전체이고, '합작'은 함께 만든 결과물이나 사업에 주로 써요.

phrases.en: This is a Korea-China joint film.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 나라나 회사가 함께 만든 영화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A film made together by several countries or companies.

phrases.en: The two countries set up a joint venture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 투자해서 만든 회사를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: A company created through joint investment.

phrases.en: Two directors collaborated to make a drama.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사로 쓰면 함께 만든다는 행동을 직접 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a verb, it describes the act of making something together.

explain_en: Two parties jointly making something (영화, 회사) When countries or companies make something together, it attaches in front, as in '합작 영화' (joint film) and '합작 회사' (joint company). '협력' (cooperation) covers any kind of helping each other, while '합작' is mostly for a jointly made product or business.

t90.ax: It is a joint Korea-Japan drama.

examples.en: My mom braided my hair.
I wear my hair in a long braid.
Braiding your hair is cool and comfortable.
My little sister is braiding the doll's hair.

examples.ko: 끈 세 가닥을 땋아서 팔찌를 만들었어요.
examples.en: I braided three strings to make a bracelet.
I will braid my hair into two plaits.

explain: 머리카락이나 끈을 보통 세 가닥으로 엇갈리게 엮을 때 써요. 'ㅎ' 받침이라 발음이 [따타], '땋아요'로 활용해요. 머리를 묶는 '묶다'와는 달라서 엮는 모양이 생겨야 땋다예요.

phrases.en: I braid my hair every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing.

phrases.example: 그 아이는 땋은 머리가 잘 어울려요.
phrases.en: Braided hair suits that child well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '땋은'으로 바꾸면 명사를 꾸밀 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Change to 땋은 to describe a noun.

phrases.example: 엄마, 제 머리 좀 땋아 주세요.
phrases.en: Mom, please braid my hair for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람에게 부탁할 때 '-아 주세요'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -아 주세요 to ask someone to do it for you.

explain_en: You use it for weaving hair or cord in an interlaced way, typically with three strands. The ㅎ final makes it sound like [따타], and the polite form is 땋아요. It differs from 묶다 (to tie); 땋다 requires the woven pattern.

examples.en: I put red nail polish on my nails.
My nail polish is chipped, so I have to redo it.

examples.ko: 주말에 친구와 같이 매니큐어를 사러 갔어요.
examples.en: On the weekend I went with a friend to buy nail polish.
This nail polish dries quickly, so it's convenient.
You can't wear nail polish at school.

examples.ko: 매니큐어 냄새가 너무 독해서 창문을 열었어요.
examples.en: The nail polish smell was so strong that I opened the window.

explain: 한국어 '매니큐어'는 손톱에 칠하는 물감 자체를 가리켜요. 발톱에 하는 것은 '페디큐어'라고 하고, 동사는 '바르다'나 '칠하다'를 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '네일'이라는 말도 많이 들려요.

phrases.en: I put nail polish on my nails.
phrases.nuance_ko: 매니큐어를 칠하는 가장 자연스러운 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural verb for putting on nail polish.

phrases.example: 친구가 내 손톱에 매니큐어를 칠해 줬어요.
phrases.en: My friend painted nail polish on my nails.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바르다'와 같은 뜻이고, 색을 입힌다는 느낌이 조금 더 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 바르다, with a slightly stronger feeling of adding color.

phrases.en: Red nail polish suits you well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색을 앞에 붙여 어떤 매니큐어인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a color in front to say which nail polish it is.

explain_en: In Korean '매니큐어' means the nail polish itself. For toenails people say '페디큐어', and the verbs are '바르다' or '칠하다'. In daily talk you also hear the word '네일'.

examples.en: If you press the cartilage in your ear, it feels soft.

examples.ko: 코는 물렁뼈로 되어 있어서 잘 구부러져요.
examples.en: The nose is made of cartilage, so it bends easily.
I ordered fried chicken cartilage.
My knee cartilage wore down, so I went to the hospital.
Cartilage is softer than hard bone.
The doctor checked the condition of the cartilage.

explain: 병원이나 수업에서는 같은 뜻의 '연골'이라는 말도 많이 써요. '물렁뼈'는 닭 연골 요리 같은 음식 이야기나 일상 대화에서도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: My knee cartilage hurt, so I went to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이지만 병원이나 수업에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but more common at hospitals and in class.

phrases.example: 저는 닭 물렁뼈를 구워 먹는 게 좋아요.
phrases.en: I like eating grilled chicken cartilage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when talking about food.

phrases.en: There is cartilage at the tip of the nose.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 어느 곳에 있는지 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain where cartilage is in the body.

explain_en: At hospitals and in classes the same thing is also called '연골'. '물렁뼈' also comes up in daily conversation and food talk, such as chicken cartilage dishes.
